chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, who said:

They wanted to sell the dates of the orchard of Abu Ziyad, so I wanted to buy them. Then I said, 'I will wait until I seek the counsel of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' So I sent Mu'adh to ask him, and he said, 'Tell him to buy them, for if he does not buy them, someone else will buy them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods if the seller is not the original owner or if someone else might buy them?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Jamil ibn Salih seeks Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) guidance on purchasing dates from a specific owner, highlighting the Shia emphasis on seeking authoritative legal clarification (*istifta'*) before commercial transactions. The Imam’s directive to proceed, noting that 'if you do not, someone else will,' underscores the validity of the sale and the principle of *istihlak* (consumption/utilization) by the buyer, ensuring the goods are secured for the community rather than lost to another party. This reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt, where the Imam’s approval validates the transaction even if the seller's status or the goods' origin might otherwise raise questions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Salih who said,

‘I wanted to sell the dates of Abu Ziyad (a plantation), so I wanted to buy it. Then I said (to myself), ‘(I shall wait) until Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> instructs me so’. So I instructed Moaz, so he asked him<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Say to him, ‘Buy it’, for if he does not buy it, someone else will buy it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih who has said the following:

“They wanted to sell the dates of ‘ Ayn of abu Ziyad (name of a place with farms that belonged to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam), and I wanted to buy it but then I decided to ask permission from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, so I asked Mu‘adh and he asked him (the Imam) about it and he (the Imam) said, ‘He can buy it because if he does not buy it someone else will buy it.’”
